Welcome! You’ll learn to describe directions using compass points and bearings. Start with this quick warm-up about the direction bearings are measured from.

A bearing is always measured clockwise from which direction?
A) East
B) South
C) North
D) West
north, so C

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

A bearing of 315° corresponds to which compass point?
A) Northeast (NE)
B) Northwest (NW)
C) Southeast (SE)
D) Southwest (SW)
hmm wait. so 315 is like... 360 minus 45 right? that's northwest i think. B
That reasoning is sound: 315° is 45° before returning to North when moving clockwise, which places it in the northwest sector. Keep the same question active and submit your chosen option.
yeah B, northwest

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

Which of the following correctly lists all eight compass points in clockwise order starting from North?
A) N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW
B) N, NW, W, SW, S, SE, E, NE
C) N, E, S, W, NE, SE, SW, NW
D) N, NE, NW, E, W, SE, SW, S
a, that one goes round clockwise from north

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

What is the bearing equivalent of the compass point Southwest (SW)?
A) 135°
B) 225°
C) 315°
D) 45°
ok so southwest is like... south and west together. south is 180 and then you go west so that's more. i think 225. B

That's it — well done. Here's another:

A seafarer records a bearing of 163° to a navigation marker. Which of the following best describes the general direction of the marker?
A) Slightly south of east (E-SE)
B) Slightly south of due south (S-SE)
C) Slightly east of due south (S-SE)
D) Slightly east of due east (E-SE)

ok so 163 is past 90 which is east, and it's before 180 which is south. so it's between east and south. that's southeast i think. and 163 is closer to 180 than to 90 so it's more south than east. so slightly east of due south. C

transcript.content:
Welcome! You’ll learn how physical, chemical, and biological weathering break down rocks in Seychelles. Start with this warm-up question.

How do burrowing organisms contribute to biological weathering?
A) They consume rock minerals and excrete acids that dissolve rock
B) They create extensive tunnel networks that fragment rock and increase its surface area to weathering
C) They transport water into deep rock fractures, promoting freeze-thaw weathering
D) They produce oxidizing compounds that rust iron minerals in rock
B

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

Lichens contribute to biological weathering by producing which of the following?
A) Mechanical pressure through rapid growth that pushes rocks apart
B) Organic acids that dissolve minerals and weaken rock surfaces
C) Water that freezes and expands within rock cracks
D) Salt deposits that crystallize on rock surfaces and break them apart
B

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

Which of the following is a characteristic that distinguishes chemical weathering from physical weathering?
A) Chemical weathering produces sand and gravel fragments of the original rock
B) Chemical weathering alters the chemical composition and mineral structure of the rock
C) Chemical weathering only occurs in tropical climates with high rainfall
D) Chemical weathering is faster than physical weathering in all environments
B

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

You observe a boulder that is mechanically intact but shows significant color change, mineral transformation, and visible oxidation. A geologist argues this is predominantly physical weathering; another argues it is predominantly chemical weathering. Who is correct and why?
A) The first geologist is correct because the boulder is mechanically intact and unbroken
B) The second geologist is correct because color change, mineral transformation, and oxidation all indicate chemical alteration of the rock's composition
C) Both are partially correct because physical and chemical weathering always occur together
D) Neither can be correct without knowing the climate history of the boulder
B

That's it — well done. Here's another:

A geologist is assessing the vulnerability of different rock types in a proposed Seychelles coastal development. Which of the following rock types would be LEAST affected by biological weathering in the tropical coastal environment?
A) Granite with abundant feldspar minerals suitable for organism colonization
B) Limestone or marble, which are readily dissolved by biological acids
C) Basalt, which is dense, lacks fractures for root penetration, and resists biological acid attack
D) Sandstone, which is porous and easily penetrated by roots and lichens
C

A bag contains 7 red marbles, 2 blue marbles, and 5 green marbles. How many marbles are in the bag altogether?

B) -1
C) 56
D) 14

A spinner has 4 green sections and 6 red sections. What is the probability of landing on green?
A) 0.6
B) 0.4
C) 0.666667
D) 2.5
B

A spinner has 2 blue sections out of 4 sections. What is the probability of spinning blue as a fraction in lowest terms? (Enter as a decimal.)

A) 14%
B) 70%
C) 12%
D) 17%
A

A probability is expressed as 1/9. Which decimal is equivalent?
A) 9
B) 0.12
C) 0.11
D) 0.22
C

The probability of an event is 4/6. Convert this to a decimal.

That's it — well done. Here's another:

A bag of Seychellois spices contains 2 packets of cumin and 3 packets of cinnamon. What is the probability of randomly selecting cinnamon?
A) 1.5
B) 0.4
C) 1.66667
D) 0.6

Event X has a probability of 20%. Event Y has a probability of 80%. Which statement is correct?
